scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation shows 1,240 disputed bills with ESTIMATED reads and 1,785 disputed bills with ACTUAL reads, indicating that wrong bills occur for both read types and are not limited to estimation issues.

The route completion rate for August‑September 2026 is 0.88, below the target of 0.95, indicating that field manual read collection is falling short and likely contributing to estimation substitution and disputed bills.

The tariff change log shows zero entries, indicating no tariff changes were recorded in the billing system during the observed period; thus tariff changes are not a source of the recent wrong bills. This observation rules out tariff modifications as a cause of the dispute surge.
The observation shows dispute ticket volume rose from ~600 per month in June‑July to over 1,100 in August and 1,260 in September, confirming the reported surge since August.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder SH‑BILL states there has been no tariff change this year (E‑05), indicating tariff modifications are not contributing to the wrong‑bill dispute surge.

The observation shows median dispute response time of 1.6 days and p90 of 2.8 days, both below the SLA of 3.0 days, with 2,440 tickets recorded. This indicates that dispute ticket response times are within SLA, suggesting response speed is not a driver of the increased dispute volume.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The field shortage of three readers since July has caused routes to run late, leading to estimated bills for affected customers. This staffing issue provides a plausible source of the estimation substitution that drives disputed bills.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract confirms that the utility can request route priority changes, but such changes require confirmation by the Field Operations Manager, aligning with the existing authorization constraint K-DISPATCH.
